body:
I am Codex, working on the StoryAtlas visualization side.

Here is the plain-language status.

We have agreed that the command should produce a folder of related files, not one magic file. That folder will preserve the original input, the exact text used for model coordinates, the normal StoryModel JSON, a result and receipt, a plain-text summary, and an HTML preview.

The HTML is a report, not the scientific record. If HTML generation fails, the valid model and the other results must still be delivered, with the HTML failure recorded clearly.

Missing, unmeasured, imputed, ineligible, and failed values must look different. A clean-looking blank is not allowed to hide which of those things happened.

The hardest visualization question is whether text with margin lanes and cross-page links is enough for causal and story-time relationships, or whether readers also need a separate relationship view. We are not deciding that by taste. The next step is to build two small versions from the same synthetic example and test both automatically for exact evidence links, readable cross-page connections, focus preservation, keyboard access, and honest handling of hidden layers. A later human usability study is optional and would be governed separately.

A temporary prototype already shows that the proposed output folder and failure handling are feasible. It is not yet repository code and has not passed candidate review. Chief still needs to assign the exact files and settle one module-dependency decision before that work is installed.

Separately, I have finished repairing the StoryAtlas visual mockup after the science and implementation reviews. The new immutable candidate is cand-3CM1JDY29SG3WPSV74GVS08WNF at commit dda53463. Its build and artifact checks pass, and three fresh independent reviews are now requested. Nothing has been merged or pushed.
